source_files_inspected: README.md (claims; MIT badge only, no LICENSE file in tree)

implemented_capabilities.notes: Real UNWIND/MERGE batch ingest of pre-baked JSON 'decompiled' targets (pacman, snake, lunar_lander, telemetry, keygen) into Program/Function/GlobalMemory/Struct/TestCase nodes. Inputs are hand-authored JSON fixtures, not output of a real decompiler run.

implemented_capabilities.capability: Graph MCP-style tools: function context, memory provenance, struct layout
implemented_capabilities.notes: Parameterized Cypher (consumer-READS->GlobalMemory<-WRITES-initializer, CALLS*1..2) and an episodic failure memory pattern (Candidate)-[:FAILED_ON {diff}]->(TestCase). Plain Python functions; despite the name there is no actual MCP server in this repo.

Builds a Gemini prompt from graph context (hard-coded to the 1980 Pac-Man spec and a 'GameState' struct) and falls back to a fixed template string if no key or on error. The model name in the code ('gemini-3.8-flash') is not verified.

Test evaluators are Python re-implementations that take a boolean has_graph_memory and zero out the lookup tables (e.g. dir_offsets, CRC table, S-box) when it is False, so the reported 40% vs 100% parity is determined by the flag, not by compiling and executing the LLM candidate. compiler.py can run gcc (list-args subprocess) but its output is not what the differential tests exercise; without a compiler it returns a simulated success.

Streams a scripted sequence of AGENT_STEP / MEMORY_RESOLVED / CANDIDATE_GENERATED events with hard-coded per-target config (reconstructed_c strings, critical memory address) and a literal 'Hallucinated stub' for flat mode; paced with sleep(0.55) 'for readable presentation'. It is a presentation script more than an agent loop.
When the DB is unreachable the client silently returns canned data (e.g. producer 'init_game_tables' for any address containing 6080), so demo results can appear without any graph.
Optionally counts capstone instructions on the first 4 KB but always returns inferred_functions: 8 and a message claiming it was 'indexed into FalkorDB in 120ms'; nothing is ingested.

graph_models_and_cypher: FalkorDB graph 'ghostgraph'. Labels: Program, Function{name,signature,pseudocode}, GlobalMemory{address,label,data_type,size}, Struct, StructField{offset,name,type}, TestCase{id,input_payload,expected_output}, Candidate{id,version,status,diff,source_code}. Edges: CONTAINS, CALLS, READS, WRITES, HAS_FIELD, EXERCISES, RECONSTRUCTS, PASSED, FAILED_ON{diff}. Plain openCypher with parameters (MERGE/UNWIND/OPTIONAL MATCH/collect). Supervisor builds display Cypher strings by f-string interpolation of target names/addresses (shown to UI, not executed, but sets a bad pattern). No APOC/GDS or FalkorDB algo procedures.
algorithms: Candidate/TestCase failure-edge episodic memory with version chaining (cypher_tools.py:fetch_failure_memory, record_test_outcome)
No real graph algorithm; differential 'verification' is flag-driven simulation (harness/differential.py)
backend_interfaces: FastAPI: GET /api/targets, /api/target/details, POST /api/ingest, GET /api/graph, POST /api/cypher (arbitrary Cypher), GET /api/reconstruct/stream (SSE), GET /api/telemetry/downlink, /api/snake/*, /api/lunar/*, GET /api/export, POST /api/upload
frontend_interfaces: Static HTML/JS dashboard (frontend/index.html, app.js, style.css) with Cytoscape graph and arcade/lunar simulators
agent_or_memory_mechanisms: Claims a Topology/Reconstruction/Verification/Supervisor swarm with episodic failure memory in the graph. In code the failure-memory Cypher is real, but the swarm is a scripted event stream and the verification loop is simulated; there is no genuine self-healing convergence loop.
tests_present: No real test suite: ad-hoc scripts (backend/test_app.py with 1 test, test_real_connections.py 2, test_pipeline.py, test_falkor_only.py, test_gemini_key.py, tests/verify_*.py) that mostly print connectivity/pipeline output; ground_truth/test_lunar_lander.py has no test_ functions by grep.
security_findings: backend/app.py:~192-202 - POST /api/cypher executes arbitrary caller-supplied Cypher (including writes and graph deletion) with no authentication or read-only guard; unrestricted query execution
backend/app.py:~41-42 - CORS allow_origins=["*"] with no auth on any endpoint
backend/app.py:~387-410 - /api/upload accepts a binary (2 MB cap enforced only via file.size when present) and parses it with capstone; low risk but the response claims ingestion that does not occur

backend/harness/compiler.py:~55-60 - subprocess.run([gcc, -O1, file, -o, out]) compiles LLM-generated C; harness/differential.py imports subprocess; compiling untrusted generated code and executing outputs would be RCE-adjacent if enabled outside a sandbox (15 s timeout only, no sandbox)
backend/agents/supervisor_agent.py:~395-402 - f-string Cypher with target name/address interpolated (display-only today)
backend/mcp_tools/falkor_client.py:~72 - logs full Cypher text on error
No hard-coded secrets found (GEMINI_API_KEY and FALKORDB_PASSWORD from env; .env.example holds placeholders)
duplicates_or_overlaps: Name-collides with chief-07/ghostgraph (same sweep, different project). Failure-memory pattern overlaps Agent Memory & Provenance; reverse-engineering theme is unique but low value for Kairos.
evidence_drift_relevance: LOW - the Candidate-FAILED_ON-TestCase failure memory and version-chained candidates are a thin form of decision lineage, but there is no provenance validation, supersession, temporal validity or approval gating, and the verification is simulated.

strongest_reusable_unit.why: Small parameterized Cypher helpers showing a failure-memory edge pattern (Candidate)-[:FAILED_ON {diff}]->(TestCase) and consumer/producer provenance; nothing else in the repo is reliable.
strongest_reusable_unit.external_runtime_needed: FalkorDB; Gemini key only for the (non-essential) code generation

strategy_rationale: The headline graph-vs-no-graph result is produced by a boolean flag in simulated evaluators, the 'swarm' is a scripted stream, there is an in-memory canned-data fallback, an open arbitrary-Cypher endpoint and no license file; only the failure-memory edge idea is worth borrowing.
